subject.title: fix: use invariant PT-PT formatting and update OpenClaw LKG

question: Should the Companion promote OpenClaw 2026.7.1 as its last-known-good default despite the linked gateway-start regression?
rationale: Selecting an LKG is a release-acceptance decision: source correctness cannot establish whether a known-regressing upstream runtime is safe for default installation.

options.title: Keep the known-good pin
options.body: Retain 2026.6.11 in this PR, land the formatting fix independently, and let the standing LKG workflow promote a subsequently proven release.

options.title: Require candidate proof
options.body: Keep the 2026.7.1 change only after current-head fresh-install, upgrade, gateway-start, and recovery evidence passes on the supported Windows/WSL path.

options.title: Accept the regression risk
options.body: Merge the new pin while explicitly owning the possibility that affected users receive a gateway that cannot start.

recommendation.title: Keep the known-good pin
recommendation.body: Retain 2026.6.11 in this PR, land the formatting fix independently, and let the standing LKG workflow promote a subsequently proven release.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the strongest combination of setup E2E, release-path, and invariant-formatting involvement.
